question: Should action authorization become a generic core tool-policy contract, and if so, what explicit capability should let an approved workflow perform an action denied to the originating agent?
rationale: The missing behavior is clear, but grammar precedence and delegated privilege determine the security boundary and cannot safely be selected from implementation convenience alone.

options.title: Generic action policy
options.body: Add a typed generic action-policy layer and require explicit capability-scoped delegation for any approved workflow that may execute otherwise denied actions.

options.title: Per-tool policies only
options.body: Keep action controls owner-specific, extend `tools.message.actions.allow` and similar settings independently, and do not add generic `tool:action` grammar.

options.title: Approval gate instead
options.body: Address outbound actions through the separate confirmation-gate design without adding static action-level allow/deny policy.

recommendation.title: Generic action policy
recommendation.body: Add a typed generic action-policy layer and require explicit capability-scoped delegation for any approved workflow that may execute otherwise denied actions.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing candidate from recent policy/message/gateway history and already provided the maintainer-facing keep-open assessment.
